oracles.claim: A ciphertext mutation that changes the decapsulation input shall not be ignored by Decaps; the derived shared secret shall change.
limitations: A single mutation may be a no-op at the algebraic level; the oracle records effectiveness

controls.negative_control: the mutation record shows the ciphertext changed

oracles.claim: A secret-key mutation that changes a used decapsulation input should change the derived shared secret.
oracles.source_reference: DeepSeek design doc Section 38.4 (relational key mutations)
limitations: The generic oracle has a ~1/q per-position false-positive floor: when the ciphertext coefficient at the mutated secret position is 0 mod q, the shared secret provably cannot change
kem_decaps_sk is not part of the security-tier oracle set

controls.positive_control: the unmutated secret key decapsulates correctly
controls.negative_control: the mutation record shows the secret key changed

oracles.claim: Encapsulation shall consume its random coins so that distinct randomness streams produce distinct ciphertexts or shared secrets.
limitations: Tests distinct-stream consumption only, not reported RNG failure
A deterministic PKE component is not the external ML-KEM contract

controls.positive_control: the deterministic tape is observed to be consumed

oracles.claim: An encapsulation key with all-zero bytes should not produce the same encapsulation output as a valid key.
limitations: The all-zero key is not a valid encapsulation key under FIPS 203; canonicality checks require the dedicated EK oracle

controls.negative_control: the mutation record shows all key bytes zeroed

oracles.claim: A mutated encapsulation key that changes the polynomial or seed fields should change the encapsulation output.
limitations: Does not check canonical 12-bit encoding; that requires the dedicated EK canonicality oracle
A mutation in an unused bit position may legitimately not change the output

controls.negative_control: the mutation record shows the public key changed

oracles.claim: Key generation shall consume its random seeds so that distinct randomness streams produce distinct keys.
oracles.source_reference: FIPS 203 Section 3.3 and Section 7.1 (key generation randomness)
limitations: Tests distinct-stream consumption only, not reported RNG failure
Low-entropy but successful RNG output is an RBG-health concern

controls.positive_control: the deterministic tape is observed to be consumed
controls.negative_control: the produced key pair is usable for a local round trip
